safi-cedvel:1-4.t:
* I'rab:
(والليل) is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم ("I swear") (إذا) is an adverbial (ẓarf) meaning "when" (ḥīna), stripped of the conditional sense, in the position of accusative, attached to (أقسم) in both places (ما) is a maṣdar particle [Note: or it is a relative noun used for a rational being in the sense of "he who", i.e. Allah, in the position of genitive, conjoined to الليل.], and the fāʿil (agent) of (خلق) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (he), i.e. Allah (اللام) is the lām of oath, a substitute for the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).
Clause: « (أقسم) بالليل ... » has no grammatical position; it is an opening clause (ibtidāʾiyya).
And the clause: «يغشى ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «تجلّى ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «خلق ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (ما).
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما خلق ... ) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the thing sworn by, الليل.
And the clause: «إنّ سعيكم لشتّى» has no grammatical position; it is the jawāb al-qasam (answer to the oath).

* Benefits:
Harmony and consonance:
Among the wonders of the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is its harmony and consonance, in a form extremely wondrous and beautiful. An example is what occurs in this noble sūra, where the frame of the sūra harmonizes with its content: the frame comes harmonious and in accord with the meanings and ideas of the sūra. The sūra opens with His saying, the Exalted (وَاللَّيْلِ إِذا يَغْشى. وَالنَّهارِ إِذا تَجَلَّى), which are two opposed images: the image of the night when it veils with its darkness, and the image of the day when it shines forth and is uncovered to anyone with eyes. Therefore the subject of the sūra came harmonious and consonant with this wonderful opening: His saying, the Exalted: (فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَعْطى وَاتَّقى وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنى) corresponds to the image of the day with its light, radiance and beauty, while His saying, the Exalted: (وَأَمَّا مَنْ بَخِلَ وَاسْتَغْنى وَكَذَّبَ بِالْحُسْنى) corresponds to the image of the night with its darkness and blackness. From here we notice the inexhaustible secrets of the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and we notice the bonds that hold its verses together in a state of wonderful concord and splendid harmony.

safi-cedvel:5-11.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive (أمّا) is a particle of condition and elaboration (من) is a relative noun in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ (subject) (الواو) is a conjunction in both places (بالحسنى) is attached to (صدّق), (الفاء) is the connecting particle of the jawāb of أمّا (السين) denotes the future (لليسرى) is attached to (نيسّر).
Clause: «من أعطى ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «أعطى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (من).
And the clause: «اتّقى ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And the clause: «صدّق ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And the clause: «سنيسّره ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The original construction: "whatever the matter may be, whoever gives... we shall ease him", and the second fāʾ was omitted for lightness.].
Verses 8-11: (الواو) is a conjunction (أمّا من بخل ... للعسرى) is like the preceding (ما) is negating [Note: or an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause يغني.], (عنه) is attached to (يغني), (إذا) is an adverbial in the position of accusative, containing the sense of condition, attached to the implied jawāb.
And the clause: «يغني ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause سنيسّره للعسرى.
And the clause: «تردّى ... » is in the position of genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.. and the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis) is omitted, its implied form being "his wealth will not avail him".

* Morphology:
(10) العسرى: a noun meaning narrowness and hardship, or the feminine elative of الأعسر, the opposite of اليسرى; its pattern is فعلى, with ḍamma then sukūn.
(11) تردّى: it contains an ʿilāl by substitution; its origin is تردّى — with a yāʾ at the end — the yāʾ, vowelled after a fatḥa, was changed to alif.

safi-cedvel:12-18.t:
* I'rab:
(علينا) is attached to the khabar of inna (اللام) is for emphasis (الهدى) is the ism (noun) of inna, accusative (إنّ لنا للآخرة) is like إنّ علينا للهدى (الفاء) is a conjunction (نارا) is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (تلظّى) is an imperfect verb from which one of the two tāʾs has been omitted (لا) is negating (إلّا) is for restriction.
Clause: «إنّ علينا للهدى» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause: «إنّ لنا للآخرة» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause: «أنذرتكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause: «تلظّى ... » is in the position of accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of (نارا).
And the clause: «لا يصلاها إلّا الأشقى» is in the position of accusative, a second naʿt of (نارا) [Note: or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from (نارا) because it has been specified by the description.
(2, 3) or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ.. or a mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being "I mean" (aʿnī).].
Verses 16-18: (الذي) is in the position of nominative, a naʿt of الأشقى «2», and the second is a naʿt of الأتقى «3», (ماله) is a first or second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the other being implied.
And the clause: «كذّب ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the first relative (الذي).
And the clause: «تولّى» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And the clause: «سيجنّبها الأتقى ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause لا يصلاها ...
And the clause: «يؤتي ماله ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative (الذي).
And the clause: «يتزكّى ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of يؤتي [Note: or it is a badal (substitute) for the clause يؤتي, with no grammatical position.].

* Morphology:
(14) تلظّى: it contains the omission of one of the two tāʾs; its origin is تتلظّى.. and it contains an ʿilāl by substitution: the yāʾ — the lām of the word — was changed to alif because it is vowelled after a fatḥa.
(17) الأتقى: it contains an ʿilāl by substitution, following the same rule as the verb تلظّى.

safi-cedvel:19-21.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive — or circumstantial — (ما) is negating (لأحد) is attached to a fronted khabar (عنده) is an accusative adverbial attached to an omitted ḥāl from نعمة [Note: or attached to (تجزى).], (نعمة) is genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ (إلّا) is for exception [Note: or in the sense of "but" (lākin)..], (ابتغاء) is accusative as a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) [Note: or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), the governing element being implied and إلّا being in the sense of لكن, i.e. "but he did that seeking the face of his Lord ..."], (الواو) is resumptive (اللام) is the lām of oath, for an implied oath (سوف) denotes the future, and the fāʿil of (يرضى) is a pronoun referring to الأتقى [Note: and likewise the pronouns in (ماله, عنده, ربّه). It is said that these verses were revealed concerning Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, when he freed Bilāl.]..
Clause: «ما لأحد ... من نعمة» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.].
And the clause: «تجزى ... » is in the position of nominative, a naʿt of نعمة.
And the clause: «سوف يرضى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the jawāb of an implied oath ... and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
